title: A `catch` clause that names a type outside the throwable tree compiles.
text: `catch (Foo $e)` for a class `Foo` that does not extend `Throwable` passes `nvs check`, and the clause can never run. `catch (int $e)` and `catch (string $e)` pass the checker and stop at `E0901` ("`is int` reached codegen"). `throw` already gives `E0780` for the same types. An interface stays allowed, since a class under `Throwable` may implement it. It closes when a class or a built-in type that no `Throwable` can be is a diagnostic in a `catch`, with a conformance case.
